_comment: Shared data for the Shipyard and the Landing Lab (approximate public figures). Served from the database as the dataset flight-data.json; edit the row to change them. engines: shared engine table. landingVehicles: the Landing Lab vehicles.

merlin-1d.name: Merlin 1D
merlin-1d.notes: Catalogue row engine-merlin. The article's infobox gives Isp 311 s for the vacuum figure; the 348 s figure belongs to the vacuum variant.

merlin-vac.name: Merlin 1D Vacuum
merlin-vac.notes: Catalogue row engine-merlin-1d-vacuum (981 kN, 348 s). Mass 500 kg and the throttle and start counts were carried over from the original table and are not re-sourced.

raptor-2.name: Raptor 2
raptor-2.notes: Changed in M0: ispSL 327 -> 347 and mass 1600 -> 1630. The article's versions table and SpaceX's 3 Aug 2024 post give 347 s sea level; 327 s is the older general figure. Dry mass 1,630 kg is the article's figure, as in the catalogue row. Not changed: thrustSL 2260 kN (article 2,256 kN), thrustVac 2500 kN (article 2,530 kN for Raptor 2) and ispVac 350 s (not stated for Raptor 2 in the article). Those three stay as they were so the sims do not move.

raptor-vac.name: Raptor Vacuum (RVac)
raptor-vac.notes: Vacuum thrust is not version-specific in the article (2018 plan 1,900 kN; 2016 plan 3,285 kN); 2,500 kN carried over. Isp about 380 s (target). Mass 1700 kg and the start count were carried over and are not re-sourced.

raptor-3.name: Raptor 3
raptor-3.notes: Added in M0 from the article (SpaceX Starship V3 announcement, 12 May 2026): 250 tf / 2,452 kN sea level, 275 tf / 2,697 kN vacuum (the article's Raptor 3 section says 2,700 kN), Isp 350 s, dry 1,525 kg. Minimum throttle 40 % is the article's Raptor figure. Start count not sourced, so flyable:false.

be-4.name: BE-4
be-4.notes: CONFLICT NOT RESOLVED in M0: the article gives 2,460 kN (original) / 2,847 kN (improved) sea level, Isp 340 s with no condition, dry mass 5,400 kg and 40-100 % throttle. The sim values above are kept so the New Glenn landing does not move; review before changing. Gimbal and cycle are from the article.

rs-25.name: RS-25
rs-25.notes: Added in M0 from the article. Dry mass 3,177 kg is the infobox figure (the body says about 3.5 t). Throttle 67-109 %. The article gives no start or restart count, so flyable:false. Not in any preset yet.

f-1.name: F-1
f-1.notes: Thrust, Isp and mass match the article. Fixed throttle and a single start were carried over (the article gives no restart count).

j-2.name: J-2
j-2.notes: The original J-2 used on Saturn IB and V (S-II 5x, S-IVB 1x). Vacuum thrust 1,033.1 kN and Isp 421 s match the article. CONFLICT: the infobox gives mass 1,788.1 kg, the specifications table 1,438 kg; 1,788 kg kept. Ignition count is the article's 3 starts (helium supply); minThrottle carried over. The J-2S is a separate engine (see j-2s).

j-2s.name: J-2S
j-2s.notes: Added in M0 (was catalogue row engine-j-2s only). Simplified, tap-off cycle, six pre-production engines test-fired, never flown. Vacuum thrust 1,138.5 kN and Isp 436 s from the article; 1,400 kg from its specifications table. Throttle and start count not sourced, so flyable:false. The Shipyard 3D model for the S-II and S-IVB J-2 engines is this engine (vehicle-glb.js maps j-2 to j-2s).

rl10.name: RL10
rl10.notes: Vacuum thrust 110 kN and Isp 465 s match the RL10B-2 in the article (110.1 kN, 465.5 s). CONFLICT: the article gives 301 kg dry for the B-2 and 170 kg for the A-4-2; 190 kg kept. Throttle and starts carried over and not re-sourced.

rutherford.name: Rutherford
rutherford.notes: Isp 311 / 343 s and dry mass 35 kg match the article. Thrust: the article gives 24.9 kN sea level and 25.8 kN vacuum, the infobox 24/25 kN and 24/26 kN; the rounded library figures are kept. Throttle and start count carried over.

rutherford-vac.name: Rutherford Vacuum
rutherford-vac.notes: Vacuum thrust 25.8 kN and Isp 343 s from the article. Start count carried over.

nk-15.name: NK-15
nk-15.notes: Added in M0 for the N1 first stage (30 engines). Thrust, Isp and dry mass from the article. Throttle and start count not sourced, so flyable:false. The article's propellant name is RG-1 (refined kerosene).

aj10-oms.name: AJ10 OMS
aj10-oms.notes: Carried over from the original table; not re-sourced in M0.

draco-cluster.name: Draco cluster (4 kN)
draco-cluster.notes: Carried over from the original table; not re-sourced in M0.

solid-motor.name: Solid motor
solid-motor.notes: Generic model, not a named motor. Carried over; not re-sourced. Thrust-time curve is gap G7.

be-3pm.name: BE-3PM (deep throttle)
be-3pm.notes: Used by the New Shepard booster in the Landing Lab. Carried over from the original table; not re-sourced in M0.

be-7.name: BE-7
be-7.notes: Lunar lander class. Carried over from the original table; not re-sourced in M0.

falcon9.name: Falcon 9 booster -- drone ship
falcon9.note: One Merlin, throttle 39-100 %: thrust-to-weight never drops below ~1.3 so it cannot hover.

falcon9lz.name: Falcon 9 booster -- landing zone
falcon9lz.note: Return-to-launch-site: a fixed concrete pad, tighter geometry, no sea state.

newshepard.name: New Shepard booster
newshepard.note: Deep-throttle BE-3PM (down to ~20 %): thrust-to-weight can drop below 1, so it can hover and ease down.

newglenn.name: New Glenn booster (3 engines)
newglenn.note: Seven-engine stage landing on three BE-4s with strakes and flaps (modelled here as grid-fin-class control).

superheavy.name: Super Heavy -- tower catch
superheavy.note: Three Raptors can nearly hover; instead of legs it is caught by the tower arms at ~70 m, so the box is a few metres wide. Experimental: the catch is still unreliable (about one flight in five).

moonlander.name: Lunar lander (BE-7 class)
moonlander.note: No atmosphere: no drag, no fins, no wind -- pure thrust control, as on the Moon.
